item.title: Residential areas hit in latest US-Israeli strikes on Tehran
item.description: Residential areas hit in latest US-Israeli strikes on Tehran Residential areas in Tehran were struck in the latest wave of US and Israeli attacks early Friday, according to Iranian media reports. Press TV said several neighbourhoods in the capital were hit, and footage showed a follow-up strike occurring as a reporter was covering the aftermath of an earlier attack. item.title: Unicef says reports indicate 180 children killed in Iran
item.description: Unicef says reports indicate 180 children killed in Iran The UN children’s agency says reports indicate that nearly 180 children have been killed in Iran since the conflict escalated. Unicef said the figures also suggest many more children have been wounded during the violence. "We urgently call on all parties to abide by their obligations under international law and ensure the protection of civilians."

item.title: Saudi Arabia downs drones near Riyadh
item.description: Saudi Arabia downs drones near Riyadh Saudi Arabia says its air defence systems have shot down three drones east of the capital, Riyadh, as the Israeli-US war on Iran continues affect regional countries. The Saudi Ministry of Defence said the drones were intercepted on Friday. "Three drones were intercepted and destroyed east of the Riyadh region," a defence ministry spokesperson said. item.title: Israel says it launched 26 waves of strikes in Beirut suburbs
item.description: Israel says it launched 26 waves of strikes in Beirut suburbs Israel’s military says it has carried out 26 waves of attacks targeting Beirut’s southern suburbs since the war began. In a statement, the Israel Defense Forces said its forces struck several sites overnight. The army said the raids targeted headquarters and 10 high-rise buildings that it claimed were "containing Hezbollah's military infrastructure". This could not be independently verified.

item.title: Iran Red Crescent says 14 medical centres damaged in attacks
item.description: Iran Red Crescent says 14 medical centres damaged in attacks The Iranian Red Crescent said 14 medical centres and nine of its affiliated facilities were damaged during recent attacks by Israel and the United States, Al Jazeera Arabic reported. The organisation said the damage occurred as strikes intensified across several parts of Iran. item.title: Iran says over 3,000 homes damaged in US-Israel attacks
item.description: Iran says over 3,000 homes damaged in US-Israel attacks Iran’s Red Crescent on Friday said more than 3,000 homes have been damaged in US and Israeli attacks across the country. The organisation’s president, Pir Hossein Kolivand, said a total of 3,643 civilian sites were affected. Kolivand said the damage includes 3,090 homes, 528 commercial and service centres, 14 medical or pharmaceutical facilities and nine Red Crescent sites. item.title: Reports say Tehran military academy struck
item.description: Reports say Tehran military academy struck A military academy belonging to Iran’s army was reportedly among the sites hit in strikes in central Tehran on Friday. Iranian media said the facility was struck as attacks continued across the capital. The strike occurred while a reporter from Iran’s state broadcaster was reporting live near the location, according to Al Jazeera.

item.description: Video: Azerbaijan President calls drone strike on airport ‘act of terror’ Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev condemned a suspected Iranian drone strike on an airport as an “act of terror.” The attack, which occurred on Thursday, left four people wounded, according to Azerbaijani authorities. Aliyev said the strike targeted civilian infrastructure and called it a serious escalation amid the widening regional conflict. item.title: US spent $3.7bn in first 100 hours of Iran war as costs mount, think tank says
item.description: US spent $3.7bn in first 100 hours of Iran war as costs mount, think tank says The first 100 hours of the US war on Iran are estimated to have cost about $3.7 billion, or roughly $891.4 million a day, according to the Washington-based Centre for Strategic and International Studies. The think tank said the early phase of the conflict is particularly expensive because it relies on advanced and costly munitions.
